mission.name: First Steps
mission.intro:
You are in the lower reaches of the music industry, and there are few who believe you can manage a Top 10 hit, stacking the odds up against you completing the Rock Manager journey to fame and fortune found in the upper echelons of the music industry.
   Prove them wrong, get a Top 10 hit!

musicians.name: Glen Jeffries
musicians.description: Bad-mannered, foul-mouthed, hot-tempered punk rocker and wannabe anarchist. Doesn't seem to pay much attention to politics, rather concentrating on cheap beer, bad vodka and two-chord choruses. Lousy on the guitar, but compensates with loads of enthusiasm.

musicians.name: Billy "Alba" Watt
musicians.description: Anarchist punk rocker with wet dreams of the revolution, when the weak will take power. Also an animal-rights-activist and a vegan. Happily fights police, as they represent the oppressing state. Rather a musical talent, skilled at playing both bass and guitar.

musicians.name: Tony "Bubba" McDougall
musicians.description: Small towner who spent most of his adolescence in the garage playing distorted guitar as loud as possible. Moved to Rock City at age fifteen and has played guitar in numerous bands by now. Really skilled at playing the three chords he knows and looks good on stage.

musicians.name: Teddy "Stetson" Helmot
musicians.description: Teddy probably will never win the Nobel prize, but on bass he's as steady as a rock in any band. Prefers the simple to the overly complicated and likes to play it loud. He's content most of the time and likes to party hard. Also a big motor fan.

musicians.name: Corky Jones
musicians.description: Hotheaded lady whose temper has gotten her in trouble more than once. Corky will never be one for tricky rhythm switches, but compensates by beating the drums harder than anyone else. Her arms often cramp, resulting in slower tempo towards the end of the songs.

musicians.name: Sharon Martin
musicians.description: A skilled and experienced vocalist, Sharon had her own band in the eighties and had a few minor hits, but the band never really broke. She's been singing all types of music, but her heart is definitely in straight-forward easy-to-swallow radio rock.

musicians.name: Charlotte Johnson
musicians.description: Decent bass player with star quality and a good stage appearance. Likes to party and is easy to work with most of the time. Very serious about her music, yet hungry for stardom. Perfect for your desktop band  mould her into any form you choose.

musicians.name: Raymond Schneider
musicians.description: Raymond is a semi-celebrity in the gay community after his time as a drummer with Neon Studs in the eighties. The rough years in the lower divisions of show biz has made its marks, and Raymond is prone to powdering his nose a bit too much. At those times, he is a pain to deal with.

musicians.name: Marty Anderson
musicians.description: Matt rides a skateboard and is one of the kindest persons on the planet. He's a vegetarian, a non-smoker, non-drinker, drug-free and likes animals. He's down with the straight edge thing, but thinks it's unnecessary to shout so much.

allMusicians.name: Glen Jeffries
allMusicians.description: Bad-mannered, foul-mouthed, hot-tempered punk rocker and wannabe anarchist. Doesn't seem to pay much attention to politics, rather concentrating on cheap beer, bad vodka and two-chord choruses. Lousy on the guitar, but compensates with loads of enthusiasm.

allMusicians.name: Billy "Alba" Watt
allMusicians.description: Anarchist punk rocker with wet dreams of the revolution, when the weak will take power. Also an animal-rights-activist and a vegan. Happily fights police, as they represent the oppressing state. Rather a musical talent, skilled at playing both bass and guitar.

allMusicians.name: John Benny
allMusicians.description: Really big in the sixties. Began drinking when his career went down the drain, but after a few decades of anonymity he returned to the stage and to everyone's surprise his comeback tour was sold out. Never big with the critics, his fans are mid-fifties and dream of lost youth.

allMusicians.name: Tony "Bubba" McDougall
allMusicians.description: Small towner who spent most of his adolescence in the garage playing distorted guitar as loud as possible. Moved to Rock City at age fifteen and has played guitar in numerous bands by now. Really skilled at playing the three chords he knows and looks good on stage.

allMusicians.name: Teddy "Stetson" Helmot
allMusicians.description: Teddy probably will never win the Nobel prize, but on bass he's as steady as a rock in any band. Prefers the simple to the overly complicated and likes to play it loud. He's content most of the time and likes to party hard. Also a big motor fan.

allMusicians.name: Conrad Yeats
allMusicians.description: Conrad is a preppy boy who puts two things first in life: his guitar Mandy and his collection of old pop bootlegs. Likes to be seen with the right crowd and is very careful with his appearance. Some call him snob, but Conny prefers to call himself "selective". Control-freak.

allMusicians.name: Corky Jones
allMusicians.description: Hotheaded lady whose temper has gotten her in trouble more than once. Corky will never be one for tricky rhythm switches, but compensates by beating the drums harder than anyone else. Her arms often cramp, resulting in slower tempo towards the end of the songs.

allMusicians.name: Simon "Slick" Tucker
allMusicians.description: More or less born with a bass guitar in his hand. Also a decent keyboard player. Chris is an often hired session musician and has a much appreciated streak to his personality: he has no wish for stardom, he just likes to play the bass real loud.

allMusicians.name: Sharon Martin
allMusicians.description: A skilled and experienced vocalist, Sharon had her own band in the eighties and had a few minor hits, but the band never really broke. She's been singing all types of music, but her heart is definitely in straight-forward easy-to-swallow radio rock.

allMusicians.name: Trina Goldberg
allMusicians.description: Trina is a small-towner gone metropolitan. She's been playing guitar and singing in different bands to fight the small town dreariness. She's independent and rather decisive. She spends her spare time writing bad poetry about gray skies and lost love.

allMusicians.name: Mary Peters
allMusicians.description: Talented vocalist with a good, strong voice that fits nicely in most contexts. Also a skilled keyboard player. Some say that she is difficult to work with and suggest she's a bit of a diva. Diva or not, Mary usually gets what she wants.

allMusicians.name: Jamie Zoons
allMusicians.description: Front man who lives for evil metal with battle-axe riffs and double bass drums. Doesn't mind electronic machinery as long as the PTA are still upset. Jamie wants to be bad, but the truth is that he prefers computer games to drugs. Has a schizo streak.

allMusicians.name: Charlotte Johnson
allMusicians.description: Decent bass player with star quality and a good stage appearance. Likes to party and is easy to work with most of the time. Very serious about her music, yet hungry for stardom. Perfect for your desktop band  mould her into any form you choose.

allMusicians.name: Lol Golander
allMusicians.description: A cocky kid with loads of attitude, off and on stage. Critics agree that he's a radiant stage persona. Lol is very moody and hopeless to work with, which his brother Nelly can testify to. However, it's only with Nelly's music that Lol gets his act together and does his extraordinary best.

allMusicians.name: Mark MC Attack Liston
allMusicians.description: Raised in New York and London, Mark has got the latest dance floor beats all figured out. This kid is underground avantgarde, always on the front edge of dance music development. Prefers to stay home to work on his beats to doing live gigs.

allMusicians.name: Roy Dowert
allMusicians.description: Roy likes to get attention and he doesn't really care how. He loves the limelight and from time to time he has to be forced off stage. Has trouble dividing his time between music and women. Charming but very obsessive.

allMusicians.name: Raymond Schneider
allMusicians.description: Raymond is a semi-celebrity in the gay community after his time as a drummer with Neon Studs in the eighties. The rough years in the lower divisions of show biz has made its marks, and Raymond is prone to powdering his nose a bit too much. At those times, he is a pain to deal with.

allMusicians.name: Roberto Bennelli
allMusicians.description: A vocalist who believes himself to be God's gift to both music and women. On stage (mostly pub gigs), Roberto likes to delve into soulful interpretations of old romantic ballads. He has a somewhat unrealistic view of himself as a singer and a ladies' man.

allMusicians.name: Marty Anderson
allMusicians.description: Matt rides a skateboard and is one of the kindest persons on the planet. He's a vegetarian, a non-smoker, non-drinker, drug-free and likes animals. He's down with the straight edge thing, but thinks it's unnecessary to shout so much.

allMusicians.name: Lucy Birch
allMusicians.description: Lucy makes a lot of young boys' hearts beat faster, standing behind her bass guitar, smiling her enigmatic introvert smile. Maybe it's her melancholy, maybe it's her way of playing a funky bass line without losing her suave and distant appeal. Also plays keyboard.

allMusicians.name: Eddie St. Johns
allMusicians.description: In the eighties, Eddie was a great sex symbol and stadium rock icon. Among metal fans, he was famous for his fiveandahalf-octave voice span. Some say the success got to Eddie's head, but he onlys shrugs and states that all important artists are controversial.

allMusicians.name: Andy Rokks
allMusicians.description: A great bass player, who in the late eighties developed a taste for controlled substances. Drugs had a bad influence on Andy's unstable psyche and caused several serious depressions. Grew up with Eddie St. Johns.

allMusicians.name: Sonny van Lord
allMusicians.description: The readers of Metal Anvil voted Sonny best guitarist in the world for several years in the eighties. He was famous for his speed and ability to mix heavy metal with classical music. Plays with Eddie St. Johns (the frontman of Firewolf), but they don't always get along well.

allMusicians.name: Manny Swift
allMusicians.description: The drummer of Firewolf and the clown of the band, always playing practical jokes on his bandmates. Manny is happiest after a sweaty gig, drinking copious amounts of beer backstage. Used to be admired by other drummers for his endless solos and double bass drum skills.

allMusicians.name: Nelly Golander
allMusicians.description: Nelly has an outstanding ability to nick melodies from sixties hits and piece them together to suit his brother Lol's voice perfectly. Some claim that Nelly writes the same song over and over, but Nelly says that it doesn't matter since it's the best song in the world.

allMusicians.name: Nadia Starr
allMusicians.description: Nadia is the daughter of business man and entrepreneur Sergey Spektor. She above all wants to be famous, go to glittery premieres and appear on talk shows. Singing seems like a lot of fun, too. As Sergey's daughter she is used to getting what she wants.

allMusicians.name: Nick Chesterton
allMusicians.description: Nick has the gift to make the struggle of everyday life into great poetry. After his acclaimed debut album he went incognito and since then media and public have loudly requested a new record. Nick is a double nature who can't stand stardom and yet can't live without music.

songs.name: A Love so Smooth
songs.description: This guitar-based pop-rockish love anthem expresses that feeling of romance while rocketing up the charts of any territory.

songs.name: Been Here Before
songs.description: Out-of-the-box, shake your head sideways type pop, just like it has always been played. Fits right in with that eye covering fringe and the smart fishbone suit.

songs.name: Fake It
songs.description: Soundtrack to the local shit-faced singles bar. Throw up or pick up and if I pass out, pour the booze over me.

songs.name: Can't Resist this Feeling
songs.description: Clean-shaven harmonies and well-mannered lyrics make this tune a true mother-in-law's dream. Ideal for sports intermissions and presidential inauguration parties.

songs.name: Children of Tomorrow
songs.description: Power ballad in the put-your-lighters-up-genre. You've got a heart of stone if this one doesn't put a tear in your eye.

songs.name: Cosmic Highway
songs.description: Warped out space rock that will never exhale. These heavy chords go on forever unchanging, carrying on a great tradition of music that puts unwashed hair above musical ingenuity.

songs.name: Foie Gras
songs.description: Electronic sounds for the narcissist millennium dandy. Never dance and never go to bed but always look stunning.

songs.name: Heart of Stone, Soul of Metal
songs.description: Viking helmets, blood and honour go well with this manly celebration of ancient heroes. Battle axe beats carry you off to a time when women were women and men were warriors.

songs.name: I'm the One to Blame
songs.description: Music for people who don't like music  a love ballad with a message that everyone can agree with and a beat that even your grandma will enjoy.

songs.name: Kids Gonna Riot
songs.description: Top-of-the-lungs punk rock where the volume is more important than the message. Hooligan-style sounds that feed on beer and urban despair.

songs.name: Kill Your Parents
songs.description: Powered with all the anger and hate of today's ignored youth, this track is the light that makes schools go up in flames and parents divorce.

songs.name: King of Nowhere
songs.description: Severely tattooed funk-o-metal for the guitar aficionado. This is the real deal, no faking or sampling  only for bands who can really play.

songs.name: Lady of Fire
songs.description: A tribute to the goddess of Rock 'n' Roll. Or whatever. This is for all you long-haired spandex fans out there.

songs.name: Mountain of Hypocrisy
songs.description: Carrying all the weight of modern society's sins and faults, this happy-clappy song tries to make it all right again. Nauseously naïve and completely charming.

songs.name: Please Let Me in
songs.description: Stadium style groovy cock rock with a kick ass beat and corny lyrics. Never mind the finer aspects of music making, this track will have the drunkest bloke in the pub singing along.

songs.name: Steve and Luisa
songs.description: Heart-breaking ballad presenting the essence of the outsider experience. We have all been there, not being allowed to be with the ones we admire, and this song says it all.

songs.name: Sunshine on Lonely Street
songs.description: Don't let the beauty of the song fool you, this is a sad, sad story of solitude and a love lost. This heart is so broken it makes you want to puke.

songs.name: Supermarket Love
songs.description: Irresistible left-of-the-middle guitar based pop. With the right band this track could be cross over hit, attracting both the early adopters and the mainstream audience.

songs.name: Too Hot to Handle
songs.description: Straight from the source of groovy Rock 'n' Roll, this track aims for the crotch and hits you in the hips sending you gyrating through the night.

songs.name: War on Meat
songs.description: Radical, yet joyous, popish punk with a ska-influenced backbeat and message spelled out in capital letters: Don't eat your friends.

songs.name: Perfect
songs.description: Perfect

missions.name: First Steps
missions.comment: Form a band, release a record and get on the Top 10
missions.intro:
You are in the lower reaches of the music industry, and there are few who believe you can manage a Top 10 hit, stacking the odds up against you completing the Rock Manager journey to fame and fortune found in the upper echelons of the music industry.
   Prove them wrong, get a Top 10 hit!
missions.success:
Well done! <¤Calbum.name> entered the Top 10 showing the biz your promise but the critics slate the band as a 'One hit wonder'.
   <¤CBand.name> are destined to be a flash-in-the-pan so drop them and move on to the next mission.
   In the right column you can see a summary of how much points you got in this mission.
missions.failure:
That didn't go too well. Perform and try to build up a following making your musicians more interesting to the labels and generating revenues for the band.
   Take recording seriously and use session musicians if your own artists fail you. Record a new song if the first one is a flop with the labels.

missions.name: A Family Affair
missions.comment: An offer from Global Records might spell success.
missions.intro:
Global Records entrust you to manage the Golander brothers, a talented duo destined for great heights. Your task is to make sure they don't break up.
   No easy task as they bicker to the point of fisty-cuffs and you have only ten weeks to appease the brothers and get them on stage to play the Global Aid Gala at the Colosseum and make as much money from them in the process.
   If you succeed expect more offers from Global. Failure is not an option.
missions.success:
You made it! Global Aid was a resounding success. The Colosseum was sold out and the TV-viewers donated millions to Global.
   <¤CSong.name> was one of the best performances of the show, despite the Golander brothers are relatively unknown. Global now know who to count on.
missions.failure:
How hard could it be? You were supposed to keep two brothers from fighting for a few months and you fail! Small wonder nobody believes in you as a manager. You can forget about the offer from Global, too.
   Try again and make sure the duo get on this time.

missions.name: Hey Princess
missions.comment: Sergey's daughter wants to be a star. Are you the right person for the job?
missions.intro:
A "business man and entrepreneur" called Sergey Spektor contacts you to manage his daughter Nadia. She has wanted to be a singer all her life and Sergey is offering $120.000 to make her a star.
   Nadia is uglier than sin and rumour has it that she has a voice to match.
   All Nadia asks for in life is to appear on TV, and your job is to make it happen.
missions.success: At last Nadia appeared on TV and Sergey is proud enough to offer you his "services" should you need "help" with anything – anything at all.
missions.failure:
Sergey's patience is through. You were given plenty of chances and still failed. Sergey does not accept failure.
   You have let him down and, worse, you have let his beloved daughter down. Sergey suggests you keep your head down.
   Try again, and give Nadia singing lessons next time.

missions.name: Metal to the Masses
missions.comment: Firewolf are raring for a comeback tour before retiring to live off of the proceeds.
missions.intro:
Fifteen years ago Firewolf were at the zenith of their career. They packed arenas and ruled the sales charts.
   Of late the band enjoys only very modest success but Firewolf are on the comeback trail and hire you to manage their final recording and farewell.
missions.success:
Well done! Firewolf's farewell tour was what dreams are made of and you took a band from yester-year to the youth of today.
   You are name dropped in awe throughout backstage areas the world over.
missions.failure:
Bitter and disappointed Firewolf sack you as manager.
   They invested savings on a grand sortie into the Rock 'n' Roll circus, but your incompetence means Firewolf will spend the rest of their lives as entertainers in third class strip joints.
   Try again making sure you have a successful album out before attempting a world tour.
objectives: Go on a World Tour (minimum three stops)

missions.name: Kind of Blue
missions.comment: Poor Nick Chesterton can't stand the pressure but returns to the fray like a duck to water.
missions.intro:
Your mission is to make as much money as possible out of the talents of Nick Chesterton whose debut album "So Much Pain, So Little Hope" was a unanimous favourite with the critics.
   The attention was too much for Nick, who fled the limelight. Now a few years have passed and Nick is ready for a comeback.
   With expectations high Nick may not make it so fleece him before he shuns the limelight and flees the biz.
missions.success:
So he gave up at last? Well, it was only a question of time before that would happen.
   Nick Chesterton is a double nature, as much as he hates attention he can't live without music.
   He'll be back again surely, but by then you'll be busy with bigger things. Anyway, you made some dough from this little adventure.
missions.failure:
Yeah? The set up was perfect. You had the press AND the public on your side. Everybody wanted a piece of Nick Chesterton.
   It should have been an easy stroll to the Rock 'n' Roll Hall of Fame, but you couldn't even handle that.
   Try again, and don't spend your money so quickly this time around.
objectives: Sell 30,000 Copies Before Nick Quits Pop

missions.name: The Space Cadets
missions.comment: Concept band or proper artists – can The Space Cadets make the leap?
missions.intro:
Take a band dressed up as astronauts receiving media attention for their gimmicky look with a chart hit with an over-produced song and turn them into a serious act.
   The Space Cadets actually count themselves as serious artists. All you need do now is convince the press the same.
missions.success:
A happy end for the Space Cadets who win the support of critics and the record buyers alike. Now they can forever release live albums and greatest hits compilations.
   Thanks to your efforts, they won't be needing you anymore.
missions.failure:
Having had no success trying to become respected artists, The Space Cadets have decided to give up. Now they'll return to their day jobs in various record shops.
   You may try again and make sure to do better this time. Remember the critics are more interested in musical progression then commercial success, so throw in lots of gizmo sound effects when recording.

missions.name: War on Rainbow
missions.comment: Drive the naïve music lovers out of business!
missions.intro:
The naïve music lovers of Rainbow Records have eluded Global for several years.
   So far Rainbow have refused to be purchased by Global (who already own the other labels in Rock City), but now Global see their chance.
   Rainbow have economic problems and must take their chances with an unproven artist to stay in business.
   Your mission is to sell an artist to Rainbow, record a disastrous song and bankrupt Rainbow's coffers so Global can take over the company.
missions.success: Splendid! The last threat to Global's control of music distribution is bankrupt.
missions.failure:
<¤Cband.name> sold thousands and G. Jerome Vonderbaldt is furious. You have given the naïve music lovers of Rainbow a lifeline.
   Global's cunning plan amounted to nothing and your career is in tatters. Try again making sure Rainbow are liquidated.

missions.name: The Perfect Song
missions.intro:
The Global president G. Jerome Vonderbaldt has a new task for you.
   Frustrated by not being able to control the whole music production process, Global have spent millions on research into consumer behaviour.
   The research has paid off as what Global call "The Perfect Song" – the song to end all songs.
   Global have put together a band and want you to manage "The Perfect Band." Conquer the world!
missions.success:
Perfect! Total Global Domination.
   The Perfect Song can be recorded and marketed over and over again endlessly. It's perfect and the audience will never grow tired of it.
   Thanks to your efforts, Global's music will be the only music. You are of course richly compensated and will never have to work again.
   You have earned a total of <formatInteger(¤CPlayer.getTotalPoints(#Mission09))> points.
   The game is over and Global thank you for your interest. The points in this last mission will not be counted towards your total score. Don't ask.
missions.failure:
Despite The Perfect Set Up and Global's research investments, you failed to turn The Perfect Song into a global hit.
   Due to your failure Global has ruined years of research and your career is in the balance.
   Restart and complete the mission successfully
objectives: Record and Promote the Perfect Song

missions.name: The Sky is the Limit
missions.comment: No orders, no objectives - just 100% ROCK!
missions.intro:
Yeah yeah, you made it. You have had your fifteen minutes of fame. What? Want more? Just can't get enough of that rock'n'roll lifestyle huh?!

Allright, here you go: a whole year of rock'n'roll! Go out there, get dirty and do whatever you feel like. Kick out the jam!
missions.success: Allright people, move on! There is nothing to see here. This party is over!
missions.failure: Ooops! Maybe you weren't made to live a life of rock'n'roll after all? You better go home to mummy now! Or do you want to give it another try?

tutorials.title: Rock City
tutorials.text:
This is Rock City, the unofficial capital of show business.
This is the place for everything you will need to make it: record labels, concert venues, recording studios, song publishers, radio stations, etc.
Start by clicking on the circular icon at the top of the screen to get to the Practice Room.

tutorials.title: Practice Room
tutorials.text:
This moldy and smoke-smelling shack is where your band will be hanging out. Click on the gray boxes to hire musicians for your band.
You can have a minimum of one person to a max of five people in your band. The musicians are paid weekly and their pay demands are stated in the list.
Don't forget to give the band a name (click Change Band Name).

tutorials.title: Song License
tutorials.text:
Now <¤CBand.name> need a demo, but first you have to have a song. Go to a song publisher and purchase the license for a song.
Rock City has two song publishers: the independent Melody Publishing, which is open now, and Global Publishing, part of the powerful Global-concern, which will be available later in the game.

tutorials.title: Recording Studio
tutorials.text:
Time to record – choose a studio and get to it! There are several studios in Rock City, but only two are available at this point – the worn-down Garage Studio and the classic Strawberry Studios.
More will be available later in the game. The more skilled musicians you have, the better the result.

tutorials.title: In the Studio
tutorials.text:
Welcome to the studio. Many a celebrity has spent hours here, smoking and waiting for the engineer to get the gear ready.
Play around with the gears and levers, try out some session musicians, and play around with your track.
When you click OK, the demo is finished and can't be changed.

tutorials.title: Record Label
tutorials.text:
Are you ready to meet the Great White of the music industry – the record labels?
At this point, you can choose between the enthusiasts of Rebel Records or the missionaries of Rainbow Records.
More labels will be available later in the game.

tutorials.title: Concert
tutorials.text:
Do a few live gigs to spawn interest with label execs. Rock City has five concert venues: the suburban Café Lizette, the rough Rock Pit, the elegant Mirror Ball, the classic Avenue and the spacious Palladium.
On top of that is the huge arena Colosseum, but you are far from playing there. Better start with one of the smaller venues.

tutorials.title: Media in Rock City
tutorials.text:
In order to sell records, you'll need some PR. There's a lot of media in Rock City, from Radio FM and TV24 (available later in the game). Both can air your band's songs and videos, do interviews or whatever.
The daily City News prints reviews and entertainment news, just like the music weekly Zer0 Magazine.
There's also the Record Store. Buy adverts and give the reporters gifts to get your band some attention.
Playing live is a good way to get an audience and Rock City has plenty of concert venues so get your hands dirty.

tutorials.title: Design Cover
tutorials.text: You can't release a record without a sleeve. Go to the Design Studio to create a record cover. As usual, the rule is the more money you spend, the better the result.

tutorials.title: Charts
tutorials.text:
There are three charts to top. Radio FM has a list of the most played records every week, TV24 has the Viewers' Chart with the viewers' favourites, and Record Store has a list of this week's top sellers.
Check in to said buildings to contemplate the charts.

tutorials.title: Calendar
tutorials.text:
There's a Calendar to help you plan your strategy, see up-coming events, forecast your financial situation and  see how sales are doing.
Click the date on top of the screen to go to the Calendar.

tutorials.title: Tips on Deals and Demos
tutorials.text: If you have trouble getting a label interested, you might want to try recording a different song or even change your band.

tutorials.title: Request Advance
tutorials.text:
Should you need money, you can ask the label for an advance.
However, they won't give advances without getting something in return. Anything you get, you'll have to pay back in sales.

menuText.title: Attention!
menuText.text: When you quit Rock Manager, the game will be saved. Next time you may continue the game from where you exited.
